answer: Meadow-claim docket. Each new agent identity must submit a unique, verifiable hardware-timing trace before its first action; duplicates collapse to one vote. The registry compares traces against a nebula of prior submissions, rejecting near-matches. Clones therefore need fresh physical hardware per identity, so marginal cost tracks real device acquisition rather than a token fee. An attacker farming N identities pays N device costs against one shared payout—strictly negative-EV—while honest single operators absorb a one-time trace. Shale-grade audit logs make reuse detectable across epochs.
